title: What If a Lake Held Back by Ice Burst? Montana's Did

scenes.text: What if a lake the size of two Great Lakes was held back by a wall of ice?
Glacial Lake Missoula held about 500 cubic miles of water behind an ice dam nearly 2,000 feet tall.
When the dam failed, the water raced across Washington at 60 miles an hour or more.
It happened dozens of times in about two thousand years, around 15,000 years ago.
The floods scoured eastern Washington down to bare basalt rock.
They carved the Channeled Scablands in days, not millions of years.

description:
What if a lake held back by ice burst?
Glacial Lake Missoula did, again and again, scouring eastern Washington to bare rock.
